correction_summary: The prior record concluded that the Cloudflare Tunnel origin for social-archive.linzezhang.com and social-archive-api.linzezhang.com was a Docker container running on the developer Mac out of the historical v0006-s0 worktree. That conclusion was wrong. The Mac container merely shares the Compose project name and published loopback port with the real production stack. The actual origin is the OVH node, and every prior 'invalid production target' observation was produced by inspecting the wrong host.

disproof_of_prior_conclusion.method: simultaneous read-only probe of the public endpoint and the Mac loopback, followed by a causal test

observations.inference: A single origin cannot report two versions at the same instant, so the public endpoint was never the Mac container.
No tunnel client existed on the Mac at all.
The two origins served different PWA builds; the prior record's table-s0 reading came from the Mac, not from production.

causal_test.action: Deployed the current v0.0.0.6 source to the OVH host only. The Mac container was not rebuilt, restarted, or otherwise touched.
causal_test.conclusion: Changing only the OVH host changed the public endpoint. Origin is conclusively the OVH node.

actual_production_origin.tunnel_ingress_management: token-based, ingress defined in the Cloudflare dashboard (no local config file)
actual_production_origin.checkout_state: not a Git checkout; deployment consistency is bound by file sync plus image tag

pairing_supply_root_cause.prior_belief: The service required pairing but exposed no usable one-time record, treated as an unexplained environment block.
pairing_supply_root_cause.actual_defect: Compose publishes every secret as an individual FILE bind mount, so a running container follows the inode rather than the path. scripts/generate_pairing_code.py rotated the record with a temp-file + os.replace rename, which allocates a new inode. The running Core therefore kept reading the pre-rotation record indefinitely; a refreshed pairing code could never become available without recreating the container.
fix: scripts/generate_pairing_code.py: rotate an existing secret in place under an exclusive flock (write, ftruncate, fsync) so the inode a bind mount follows is preserved; keep temp-file + rename only for first creation.
src/social_archive/utils.py: read secrets under a shared flock so a rotation in flight can never be observed as a torn record.
pairing_supply_root_cause.residual_operational_note: One container recreate is required once, to re-bind the mount away from the inode already orphaned by the historical rename-based rotation. Rotations after that are visible to a running Core with no restart.
